Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

(p-3) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah al-Hashr

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) had previously given a discussion on the meaning of tasbih (glorification) at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with David, and the birds; and We were doers [of that].﴾ [al-Anbiya: 79]

He (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Tasbih in the language means distancing from evil, and in the terminology of the Sharia it means declaring Allah, exalted is He, free of everything that is unfitting to His perfection and majesty. He (may Allah have mercy on him) cited the texts on the glorification of all created things.

He said at the end of the topic: The apparent meaning is that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and We were doers [of that]﴾ emphasizes His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with David, and the birds﴾, and what necessitates this emphasis is that the subjugation of the mountains and their glorification is a wondrous matter, contrary to custom, liable to be denied by the disbelieving ignorant. [From the fourth part, p. 337, and he mentioned additional points on this at the beginning of surah al-Hadid.]

In the study notes of what he dictated (may Allah have mercy on him) during the study term on the beginning of surah al-Jumu'a: ﴿Glorifies Allah whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [al-Jumu'a: 1] He said: Tasbih is tanzih (declaring free of imperfection), and "ma" is used for non-rational beings, because non-rational beings predominate by their number. It would have been possible to suffice with referring to what he (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him) mentioned, but the need now calls for more explanation to the extent possible, because the topic is connected to a matter of the utmost importance, and we live today in an age dominated by secularism and materialism, so we present what we can, hoping for greater clarification.

The root of tasbih is from the root s-b-ḥ, and swimming (sibaha) and tasbih share the root, so there is a commonality in the basic meaning. A swimmer in water is saved by it from drowning; likewise the one who glorifies Allah and declares Him free (of imperfection) is saved from shirk and lives through remembrance and glorification of Allah, exalted is He.

The verb has come here in the past form: (sabbaha lillah), as it came at the beginning of surah (p-4) al-Hadid.

Abu Hayyan said there: When Allah, exalted is He, commanded creation to glorify at the end of surah al-Waqi'a, meaning in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty. So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 95-96], He came at the beginning of the immediately following surah with the past verb, to indicate that the glorification commanded has already been performed, and that all that is in the heavens and the earth has committed to it. End of quote.

It is known that the verb also came in the present form, as at the end of this surah: ﴿Glorifies Him whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [al-Hashr: 24], and at the beginning of surah al-Jumu'a: ﴿Glorifies Allah whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Jumu'a: 1], and at the beginning of surah al-Taghabun: ﴿Glorifies Allah whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; to Him belongs dominion and to Him is praise, and He is over all things competent.﴾ [al-Taghabun: 1]. This form indicates permanence and continuity.

Indeed, the verb has even come in the imperative form: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1], ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 74].

And the root came as a verbal noun: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra: 1], ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [al-Rum: 17], all of which indicates the permanence and continuity of glorifying Allah, exalted is He, by all His creation, just as He, glorified Himself, and His angels and messengers glorified Him, as will come its explanation, Allah willing, exalted is He.

The "ma" in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is among the forms of generality, and its basic use is for non-rational beings, though it may be used for the rational when they are treated as non-rational, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [al-Nisa: 3]. Its use here for non-rational beings is by predominance, due to their number, as already mentioned, so it includes the rational a fortiori.

Among what draws attention is that the glorification mentioned in contexts of generality in the Qur'an is all attributed to "ma" and not "man," except in one place: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him﴾ [Nuh: 44]. This is evidence of the comprehensiveness of "ma" and its generality mentioned above, because He, glorified is He, first attributed glorification to the seven heavens and the earth explicitly by their own essences, and they are non-rational beings with what is in each of them of orbits, stars, constellations, mountains, valleys, and paths; then He conjoined to the non-rational beings, with the form "man," which is specific to rational beings, saying: ﴿and whoever is in them﴾. Although "man" may be used for non-rational beings when they are treated as rational, as in the words of the poet:

O flock of sand grouse, will anyone lend me his wing, that I may fly to the one whom I have loved?

Thus the attribution of glorification encompassed everything within the scope of the heavens and the earth, rational and non-rational, and this comprehensiveness is confirmed by His explicit saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies [Allah] by His praise﴾ [al-Isra: 44], and the word "thing" (shay') is the most general of generals, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6]. It thus includes the heavens and the earth, the angels, mankind, the jinn, the birds, animals, plants, trees, clods, and every creature of Allah, exalted is He.

The Noble Qur'an and the purified Sunnah affirm glorification from each of these individually.

First: Allah's glorifying Himself: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra: 1], ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾, ﴿And to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at dusk and when you are at noon﴾ [al-Rum: 17-18], ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾ [al-Anbiya: 22].

Second: the glorification of the angels: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it those who will cause corruption therein and shed blood while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?"﴾ [2], and His saying: ﴿And you see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting with praise of their Lord﴾ [al-Zumar: 75], and ﴿They glorify [Allah] by night and day; they do not slacken﴾ [al-Anbiya: 20].

Third: the glorification of thunder: ﴿And the thunder glorifies [Allah] with His praise﴾ [al-Ra'd: 13].

Fourth: the glorification of the seven heavens and the earth: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth glorify Him﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

Fifth: the glorification of the mountains: ﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to exalt [Allah] with him at evening and sunrise﴾ [Sad: 18].

Sixth: the glorification of the birds: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with David, and the birds﴾ [al-Anbiya: 79].

(p-6) Seventh: the glorification of man: ﴿So glorify [Allah] with the praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr: 98], ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 74], ﴿So he came out to his people from the prayer niche and inspired to them, "Glorify [Allah] morning and evening"﴾ [Maryam: 11].

This is the explicit attribution of glorification to all these worlds, detailed, explained, and clear.

Similar to glorification, and its counterpart, prostration, has come attributed to other worlds, namely the remainder of what exists in this universe of kinds and categories, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the creatures, and many of the people?﴾ [al-Hajj: 18].

It is noted here that He, exalted is He, first attributed prostration to "whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth," and "man" is for rational beings, i.e., the angels, mankind, and the jinn; then He conjoined to the rational beings non-rational ones by their names: the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and the creatures. This is a comprehensiveness that leaves no existent among the existents, nor an atom in a wilderness, unincluded.

After explaining this comprehensiveness and generality comes the topic of the general that remains general, and the specified general, and whether the generality of "ma" here remains on its generality or has been affected by specification.

A group of scholars, including Ibn 'Abbas, said: the generality remains on its generality, and the word tasbih is to be taken in its literal sense of declaring free and praising.

Some said: the generality remains on its generality without any specification entering it, but glorification varies, and each has its own kind: for rational beings it is by remembrance, praise, and glorification, as with humans, angels, and jinn; and for non-rational beings, whether animals, birds, plants, or inanimate things, it is by indication, by bearing witness to itself and showing that Allah, exalted is He, is Creator and Capable.

Others said: specification has entered it.

Al-Qurtubi related from 'Ikrimah, who said: "The tree glorifies, but the pillar does not glorify." Yazid al-Raqashi said to al-Hasan, while they were eating and the tablecloth had been brought: "Does this tablecloth glorify, O Abu Sa'id?" He said: "It once glorified," meaning that glorification is from what is living or growing, whether animals or plants, and anything else is not. Al-Qurtubi said: this view is supported from the Sunnah by what is established from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding placing a green palm frond on a grave, and his saying ﷺ about it: "Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as they have not dried up." That is, because of their glorification; when they dry, their glorification ceases. End of quote.

The correct position among all of this is the first, which Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, stated, and which the Noble Qur'an testifies to, for several reasons:

First: the explicit saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

Second: that what led them to say that glorification is by indication is the judgment of the senses and intellect, when they did not witness it and the intellects could not conceive it; but Allah, exalted is He, negated here the judgment of the sensory intellect, and warned the intellect with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿but you do not understand their glorification﴾.

Third: the saying of Allah, exalted is He, concerning the prophet of Allah, David, peace be upon him: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with David, and the birds﴾ [al-Anbiya: 79], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify with him at evening and sunrise﴾ [Sad: 18]. For had their glorification with him been glorification by indication, as they claim, David, peace be upon him, would have had no distinction over others.

Fourth: Allah, exalted is He, informed that all these worlds have a complete perception like human perception or greater than it. He, exalted is He, said of the heavens, the earth, and the mountains: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was ever unjust and ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72]. Thus Allah, exalted is He, affirmed for these worlds perception and apprehension of bearing the Trust, while He recorded against man injustice and ignorance in bearing it. This offering was not mere subjugation, nor this refusal mere passivity, but from complete perception, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [both] willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly, obedient."﴾ [Fussilat: 11]. Thus they are two groups belonging to Allah, and they refused to bear the Trust out of apprehension of it.

At the end of this noble surah, surah al-Hashr, is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of Allah﴾ [al-Hashr: 21]. Similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that, so they were like stones or even harder. And indeed, among stones are those from which rivers gush forth, and indeed, among them are those that split and water emerges from them, and indeed, among them are those that fall down from fear of Allah﴾ [al-Baqara: 74], and this is the very perception, greater than human perception.

(p-8) And in the hadith: "No stone, clod, or tree hears the voice of the muezzin but it will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection." So with what would it bear witness if it did not perceive the adhan and the muezzin?

And concerning the perception of birds, Allah the Exalted says about the hoopoe, addressing the Prophet of Allah Sulayman: ﴿I have encompassed [knowledge] of that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾ ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne﴾ ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made attractive to them their deeds and has averted them from the way, so they are not guided﴾ [an-Naml: 22-24].

In this context there are ten matters that the hoopoe perceived and expressed to the Prophet of Allah Sulayman:

The first: his perception that he had encompassed what was not within the knowledge of Sulayman.

The second: his knowledge of Sheba specifically, to the exclusion of others, and his coming from it with certain news that admits no doubt.

The third: his knowledge that a woman had been placed over them, while he disapproved of this for them.

The fourth: his perception of what Sheba had been given of worldly provisions, of all things.

The fifth: that she has a great throne.

The sixth: his perception of what they were engaged in, namely prostrating to the sun instead of Allah.

The seventh: his perception that this is shirk (associating partners) with Allah the Exalted.

The eighth: that this is from Satan's making their deeds attractive to them.

The ninth: that this is straying from the upright path.

The tenth: that they are not guided.

Sulayman was convinced by the hoopoe's perception of all of this, and he said to him: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or are among the liars﴾ [an-Naml: 27]. He gave him a letter and sent him as an envoy to Bilqis and her people: ﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then turn away from them and see what they return with﴾ [an-Naml: 28]. It was a successful mission, which brought them (p-9) to submission, as Allah says about her: ﴿And I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [an-Naml: 44].

Likewise is what came concerning the ant, in Allah's saying about it: ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive"﴾ [an-Naml: 18]. It perceived the army's approach, that it belonged to Sulayman and his soldiers, and it perceived their large number, and that it and the ants had to avoid the path and enter their dwellings. This perception on its part caused Sulayman, peace be upon him, to smile laughing at its words. And it had a speech that Sulayman, peace be upon him, understood.

The Sunnah has established that animals perceive unseen matters as well as observed ones, as in the hadith in the Muwatta' concerning the virtue of Friday: "On it Adam was created, on it he was made to dwell in Paradise," up to his saying ﷺ: "On it the Hour will occur, and there is no creature on earth except that it listens attentively from the dawn of Friday until sunrise, out of apprehension of the Hour, except the jinn and mankind." This is perception and apprehension from the animal, and faith in the unseen, which is the establishment of the Hour; and apprehension of the Hour is greater in animals than in humans.

And the story of the camel that bolted from its people and submitted to him (ﷺ), until Abu Bakr said, "It is as if it knows that you are the Messenger of Allah." He (ﷺ) said, "Yes, indeed there is nothing between its two lava-plains (the two stony tracts of Medina) but that it knows that I am the Messenger of Allah."

All of this establishes that animals have perception of the sensible, and of the unseen, a perception not less than that of humans. So what prevents affirming their glorification in reality, according to what Allah knows of them? The text has explicitly stated the glorification attributed to them, that it is glorification of praise and not mere indication, as in Allah's saying: ﴿And the thunder glorifies [Allah] with His praise﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 13], and He joined it with the glorification of the angels: ﴿and the angels, out of fear of Him﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 13]. This is a clear text on the point at issue and an affirmation of the type of glorification that is intended.

Fifth: The Muslims have witnessed inanimate things speaking in glorification, and they have heard it sensibly, such as the glorification of the pebbles in his (ﷺ) palm, and the moaning of the trunk for the Prophet (ﷺ) until everyone in the mosque heard it. And what he (ﷺ) reported: "Indeed I know a stone in Makkah which used to greet me whenever I passed by it." And what is established for one individual is established for the rest of its kind, as is known in the principle of "the one by genus" and "the one by species."

Of the same kind, and greater than that, is what al-Bukhari narrated in the Book of Virtues from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) ascended Uhud, with Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, and it trembled with them, so he said: "Be still, O Uhud, for upon you are a Prophet, a siddiq (truthful one), and two martyrs."

(p-10) And in the Muwatta' of Malik: When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from a journey, Uhud came into view for them, and he said: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it."

So this is one of the great mountains of Medina, which trembles at the ascent of the Prophet (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, and he (ﷺ) addresses it with the address of the intelligent, perceiving one: "Be still, O Uhud, for upon you are a Prophet, a siddiq, and two martyrs." It recognizes the Prophet, recognizes the siddiq and the martyr, and so it is still. By what law then was its trembling? By what reasoning was his address? In what sense was its stillness? Then behold, he establishes for it the mutual love with his saying: "It loves us and we love it."

And if we examine the views of those who restrict this general statement of the glorification of inanimate things and the like, we will find that they have no standpoint except that the senses have not witnessed any of that. We have cited examples establishing this for all kinds, and the shaykh's earlier admonition about confirming this by Allah's saying: ﴿And We were doers [of it]﴾ [al-Anbiya': 79] is a rebuttal of their rejection of it.

Among the Qur'anic proofs in this context is what occurs in the context of Allah's saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Allah] by His praise﴾ [al-Isra': 44]. Following it is Allah's saying: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed barrier﴾ [al-Isra': 45]. This is a text that refutes those who argue from the senses, because Allah the Exalted informed that He placed between the Messenger (ﷺ) in that state and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a barrier that screens him from them, and this barrier is concealed from their eyes, so they do not see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because he is screened from them, and they do not see the barrier, because it is concealed. And this is the correct reading of this verse.

Some rhetoricians have said concerning it that "concealed" here means "concealing." It is said to them that making "concealed" mean "concealing" is a repetition of the meaning of "barrier," because Allah's saying: ﴿We placed between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a barrier﴾ [al-Isra': 45] already means "concealing," that is, it screens him from those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and there is no added meaning in this, nor a great miracle. Rather, the miracle lies in the barrier being concealed from their eyes. In this there is confirmation of both meanings: his (ﷺ) being screened from them, and the barrier's concealment from their eyes. This is more emphatic in protecting him (ﷺ) from them, because if the barrier were visible, meaning merely concealing while being visible, they might have broken through it against him. And it is stronger as a miracle, because if the barrier were visible, it would be like the screening of anyone else among people. But the true miracle in it is that it is concealed from their eyes, and this is what Ibn Jarir preferred.

The story of the wife of Abu Lahab has come in detail confirming what we have mentioned, as Ibn Kathir related it: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the surah, ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ up to ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of fiber﴾ [al-Masad: 1-5], the wife of Abu Lahab came with a stone in her hand, and she was shrieking, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, near the Ka'bah. He said to him: "I fear that she will harm you." He (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted protects me from her," and he recited Qur'an. She came and stood over Abu Bakr and said: "Your companion has satirized me." He said: "No, by the Lord of this House, he is not a poet, nor a satirist." She said: "You are believed," and she departed. That is, she did not see him while he was sitting with Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

So is it said that there is no barrier because it is concealed and not witnessed? Or do we affirm it as Allah the Exalted informed, He who is capable of all things? In light of this, and after affirming it, we say: What is the difference between affirming the literal reality of Allah's saying here, "a concealed barrier," and His saying: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra': 44]? In both contexts there is an affirmation of a matter that we do not perceive by the senses: glorification we do not comprehend, and the barrier we do not see.

We have presented these examples, even with some repetition, because of the influence that some have received from the claims of materialists and secularists, who affirm only the sensible, so that the reader gains further clarity, and knows that the believer, by his faith, attains knowledge of what others do not know, and his horizon extends beyond the sensible, and he knows that beyond the boundaries of matter are worlds whose features the intellect falls short of, yet the believer affirms them.

The Prophet (ﷺ) has laid out for us the correct path in such a context of affirmation and faith, as in Sahih al-Bukhari, that the Prophet (ﷺ) "prayed the dawn prayer, then turned to the people and said: 'While a man was driving a cow, he mounted it and struck it, and it said: We were not created for this; we were only created for plowing.' The people said: 'Glory be to Allah! A cow speaks?!' He said: 'I believe in this, I and Abu Bakr and Umar,' though they were not there. And while a man was among his sheep, a wolf attacked and took a sheep from them, and he pursued it until it seemed he had rescued it from it. The wolf said to him: 'You rescued it from me; so who will take care of it on the day of the predator, the day when it has no shepherd but me?' The people said: 'Glory be to Allah! A wolf speaks!' He said: 'I believe in this, I and Abu Bakr and Umar,' though they were not there."

In this explicit text there is the speech of the cow and the speech of the wolf, with intelligible words of the kind characteristic of rational beings, contrary to custom, at which the people marveled and glorified Allah in magnification of what they heard. But the Messenger (ﷺ) dispels this wonder by declaring his faith and assent, and he includes with him Abu Bakr and Umar, even though both were absent from the gathering, because he knew that they would not deny what was established by a sound chain, merely because the intellect finds it strange.

Here it is said to those who deny the literal glorification: what prevents it? Is it a matter of power, or is it the intellect's remoteness because of the absence of sensory perception?

As for the first, it is impossible, because Allah is capable of all things. He brought forth for the people of Salih a pregnant she-camel from the inside of the hard rock, and He made the pebbles in the palm of his (ﷺ) speak.

As for the second, there is no way to it until one awaits its perception, and the intellect judges it. For Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra': 44].

Thus nothing remains but faith, which is most like the unseen matters: a faith of assent and affirmation, not of modal specification and perception. The Creator of beings knows best their state and that for which He created them.

Therefore we must believe in the glorification of everything in the heavens and the earth, even if it is strange to the intellect, because its Creator, glorified be He, has informed us of it, and we have witnessed the example audibly from some of its kinds.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 2 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes﴾.

The exegetes unanimously agreed that it refers to the Banu al-Nadir, except for an opinion of al-Hasan that it refers to the Banu Qurayzah. This opinion was refuted on the grounds that the Banu Qurayzah did not leave, nor were they exiled, but rather they were killed.

This surah has been named the Surah of "Banu al-Nadir," as related by al-Qurtubi from Ibn 'Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Hashr?" He said: "Say Surat al-Nadir." They were a group of Jews from the descendants of Harun (peace be upon him), who settled in Madinah during the trials of the Children of Israel, awaiting Muhammad ﷺ.

The exegetes agreed that the Banu al-Nadir had made a treaty with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they would be neither against him nor with him. When he prevailed on the day of Badr, they said: "He is the Prophet whose description is in the Torah; his banner is never turned back." But when the Muslims were defeated on the day of Uhud, they doubted and broke the covenant. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf went out with forty riders to Makkah, and they made an alliance with Quraysh at the Ka'bah. Jibril informed the Messenger ﷺ of this, so he ordered the killing of Ka'b, and Muhammad ibn Maslamah killed him by treachery; he was his foster-brother. The Prophet ﷺ had also discovered their treachery when he went to them regarding the blood-money of the two Muslims whom 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri had killed on his return from Bi'r Ma'unah; they then resolved to drop a stone on him ﷺ, but Allah protected him.

When Ka'b was killed, he ﷺ ordered a march against them and demanded that they leave Madinah. They asked him for a respite of ten days in order to prepare for departure, but 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy secretly sent to them: "Do not leave the fortress; I will support you with two thousand fighters from my people, and with the help of the Banu Qurayzah and their allies from Ghatafan, or they will go out with you." So they fortified themselves and held out behind their internal defences, and he ﷺ besieged them for twenty-one nights.

It was also said: they agreed to betray the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said to him: "Go out with thirty of your companions, and thirty of us will come out to you, so that they may hear from you; if they believe, we will all believe." He did so, and they said: "How can we understand while we are sixty? Go out with three, and three of our scholars will come out to you." They did so, and they concealed daggers, intending to assassinate him. But a sincere woman among them sent to her brother, who was a Muslim, and informed him of what they intended. He hastened to the Messenger ﷺ and whispered to him the news of them before he reached them. When the next day came, he went out against them with the battalions and besieged them for twenty-one nights. Then Allah cast terror into their hearts, and they despaired of the support of the hypocrites which Ibn Ubayy had promised them. They sought reconciliation, but he ﷺ refused except for their exile, on condition that each three households might carry on one camel whatever goods they wished, except the metal fittings. They then carried whatever they could, even the doors of the houses, tearing down their own dwellings and taking with them what they were able to carry.

We have presented a summary of this story in the context of the occasion of revelation of this surah, because all the meanings of this surah revolve around it. As the Imam Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his treatise "Usul al-Tafsir": knowing the occasion of revelation helps in understanding the tafsir (exegesis). And so that the Muslims may know the extent of the treachery to which the Jews are inclined, and the methods of evasion they followed; how similar is the tonight to the last night.

What is characteristic of the methodology of the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, in al-Adwa' is his saying, the Exalted: ﴿He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes﴾, where he attributed their expulsion to Allah, the Exalted, despite the existence of the siege of the Muslims against them.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, had previously made a similar point at His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah turned back those who disbelieved in their rage, not attaining any good﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25]. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said there: "He, glorified and exalted, mentioned that He [turned back] ﴿the people of him who disbelieved and denied﴾ etc., and did not explain the cause by which He turned them back, but He, glorified and exalted, explained that in His saying: ﴿So We sent against them a wind and hosts you did not see﴾ [al-Ahzab: 9]." End of quote.

Here too, in this verse, He attributed their expulsion to Himself, despite the siege of the Muslims against them, and He explained the true cause of their expulsion in His saying: ﴿So Allah came at them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts﴾. This is among the most important causes of their expulsion, because they were in a position of strength behind the fortresses; the believers did not expect their departure, and they themselves thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah. So Allah came at them from where they did not expect. This expulsion was from Allah to them by a prior promise from Allah to His Messenger in His saying: ﴿And if they believe in the like of what you have believed, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, they are only in dissension, and Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137].

By this expulsion the sufficiency of Allah for His Messenger ﷺ against them was realized; He had sufficed him against them by their expulsion from their homes. So their expulsion was truly from Allah, the Exalted, and by a prior promise from Allah to His Messenger ﷺ.

He confirmed this by His saying, addressing the Muslims specifically: ﴿So you did not press upon it with horse or camel; but Allah gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾ [al-Hashr: 6]. The empowerment of the Messenger ﷺ is by what he ﷺ explained in his saying: "I have been supported with terror for a distance of a month," which accords with His saying: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾ [al-Ahzab: 26].

The entire context here agrees exactly with the context in Surat al-Ahzab concerning the Banu Qurayzah, in His saying: ﴿And He brought down those who backed them from the People of the Book from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts; a party you killed and a party you took captive﴾, and ﴿and caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth﴾ [al-Ahzab: 26-27]. By this the reality of attributing their expulsion to Allah, the Exalted, became manifest: ﴿So Allah came at them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts﴾. Likewise He, the Exalted, is the One who turned back those who disbelieved in their rage, not attaining any good, by sending upon them winds and hosts; He is the One who sufficed the believers in fighting; He is the One who brought down the Banu Qurayzah from their fortresses and caused the believers to inherit their homes and wealth. Allah is ever competent over all things.

What confirms all this is the concluding phrase at the end of the verse, calling for reflection and admonition from what Allah did to them: ﴿O you of vision﴾ [al-Hashr: 2], meaning: by the expulsion of those who disbelieved from their fortresses, their homes, and their places of strength, you did not think they would leave because of the weakness of your power; ﴿and they thought that their fortresses would protect them﴾ by their strength and protection; but Allah came at them from where they did not expect, and cast terror into their hearts, so they could not remain. The true nature of their expulsion from their homes was from Allah, the Exalted.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿for the first gathering﴾.

There has been difference over the meaning of "al-hashr" (gathering) in this verse, and accordingly there has been difference over the meaning of "al-awwal" (first).

It was said: the intended "hashr" is the place of gathering (ard al-mahshar), which is al-Sham (Syria).

It was also said: the intended "hashr" is the assembling (al-jam').

Those who held the first view relied on reports including what Ibn Kathir related from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Whoever doubts that the place of gathering is here, meaning al-Sham, let him recite this verse: ﴿He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes for the first gathering﴾." And what Abu Hayyan related in al-Bahr from 'Ikrimah as well, and al-Zuhri, and he cited the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to the Banu al-Nadir: "Go out." They said: "To where?" He said: "To the land of the gathering." On this view, the "firstness" is locational: the first place of the land of gathering, which is the land of al-Sham; and its first parts are Khaybar and Adhri'at.

It was also said: the "hashr" is in its literal sense, which is assembling. Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit: "al-Hashr is the gathering for heading towards a certain direction." From this meaning it was said: the "hashr" is the Messenger ﷺ's mustering of the battalions for fighting them; and this was his first gathering against them and his first fighting against them. On this view the "firstness" is temporal, and it implies a gathering after it. It was said: this is the gathering of 'Umar against them at Khaybar; it was said: it is a fire that drives people from the east to the west, and this is a hadith in the Sahih; and it was said: it is the Resurrection.

However, these meanings are more general than the point of dispute, because the fire mentioned and the Resurrection are not specific to the Jews nor to the Banu al-Nadir alone. Among what the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, indicated is that among the types of clarification is deriving one of the meanings from its being the predominant usage in the Qur'an, and he gave an example of it in the introduction with His saying: ﴿Surely I shall prevail, I and My messengers﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21]. Some scholars said that the intended "ghalabah" (prevailing) here is prevailing by argument and clarification, whereas the predominant usage in the Qur'an is prevailing by the sword and the spear; and this is clear evidence that this prevailing is included in the verse, because the best way to clarify the Qur'an is by the Qur'an.

(p-16) Here in this verse, the predominant usage of the Qur'an, indeed its general usage of "hashr," is for assembling. Then the intended meaning of "hashr" is clarified by His sayings: ﴿And his hosts were gathered (wa-hushira) for Sulayman, of the jinn, the men, and the birds﴾ [al-Naml: 17]; and His saying: ﴿And We shall gather against them every thing face to face﴾ [al-An'am: 111]; and His saying about the Prophet of Allah Dawud: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah), each returning to Him﴾ [Sad: 19]; and His saying, the Exalted, about Pharaoh: ﴿He said: "Your appointment is the Day of Adornment, and that the people be gathered in the forenoon"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 59]; and His saying: ﴿They said: "Delay him and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers"﴾ [al-A'raf: 111]; and His saying: ﴿Then he gathered and called out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 23]. All of these carry the meaning of assembling.

When it is used in the sense of the Day of Resurrection, it comes accompanied by something that indicates it, and this is the case in all the Qur'an's usages for this meaning, such as His saying: ﴿And you see the earth bare, and We shall gather them﴾ [al-Kahf: 47], and that is on the Day of Resurrection, due to the earth's being laid bare;
• and His saying: ﴿The Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾ [Maryam: 85], and that is on the Day of Resurrection, due to its being restricted by the word "Day";
• and His saying: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and We shall gather the criminals that day, blue-eyed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102];
• and His saying: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [al-Takwir: 5];
• and His saying: ﴿And the Day the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, and they will be marshalled﴾ [Fussilat: 19];
along with other instances restricted by what specifies the intended meaning of "hashr," which is the Day of Resurrection.

When it is unrestricted, it means mere assembling, as in the examples mentioned above. Accordingly, the intended meaning of His saying: ﴿for the first gathering﴾ is that the preponderant reading is "for the first assembling," and the "firstness" is temporal and actual. The first assembling of the Jews occurred, and it was followed by another assembling of their brethren, the Banu Qurayzah, one year later, and it was followed by another assembling at Khaybar. We have already noted the linkage between the expulsion of the Banu al-Nadir from their homes and the bringing down of the Banu Qurayzah from their fortresses. Likewise He linked the gathering of these with those; except that these were exiled and expelled, whereas those were killed and enslaved.

Note
That "hashr" means assembling does not conflict with their departure being toward the outskirts of al-Sham, because the primary aim was their gathering to leave Madinah, and afterward they headed to al-Sham or elsewhere.

Some scholars have derived that their direction was toward al-Sham from His saying: (p-17) ﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs, or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath; and the command of Allah is ever executed﴾ [al-Nisa': 47]; because the context concerns the People of the Book, and the allusion to the people of the Sabbath applies more closely to them.

Some commentators said: the "wujuh" here refers to their dwelling in Medina, and its "tamsh" (obliteration) is the change of its landmarks, and "radd 'ala adbarihim" (turning them back on their heels) means to the lands of al-Sham from which they had first come when they left al-Sham for Medina, awaiting Muhammad (ﷺ). Abu Hayyan related this, and al-Zamakhshari considered it good (hasannahu).
* *
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect﴾.
"Ata" (came/came upon) has several meanings: among them, the meaning of coming, among them the meaning of warning, and among them the meaning of surprising attack (al-mudahamah).
Al-Razi has imagined that it belongs to the category of the attributes, and he said: "The second issue: His saying, 'So Allah came upon them' cannot be taken according to its apparent meaning by the agreement of the majority of rational people; this indicates that the door of interpretation (ta'wil) is open, and that diverting verses from their apparent meanings according to the requirements of rational proofs is permissible." End of quote.
This is from him according to his principle in interpreting the verses of the attributes. What suffices to refute it is that it is based on the requirements of rational proofs, and it is known that reason has no place in the matter of the attributes of Allah, exalted is He, because they are above the levels of intellects: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11], and they do not encompass Him in knowledge, glorified and exalted is He.
As for the meaning of the verse, the context of the Qur'an indicates that this kind of context does not belong to the category of attributes, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah came upon their building from its foundations﴾ [al-Nahl: 26], meaning He demolished it and uprooted it from its foundations. Similar to it is: ﴿There came upon it Our command by night or by day﴾ [Yunus: 24],
• and His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41],
• and His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 44].
In the hadith from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning contagion (al-'adwa): "I said: you have been struck (utita), i.e., you have been afflicted, and your perception has changed, so you imagined as correct what is not correct."
It is said: "Utiya fulan" with a dammah on the hamzah and a kasrah on the ta' when the enemy has encircled him (adhalla 'alayhi al-'aduw). From this is their saying: "The cautious one is attacked from his place of safety" (min ma'manihi yu'ta al-hadhar). So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect﴾ means: He seized them, overtook them, and took them by surprise from where they did not expect, through the killing of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and their siege, and the casting of terror into their hearts.
There is another position in Surat al-Baqarah that supports what we have mentioned here, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command. Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109]. So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾, while it is in the context of the People of the Book, and they are the very ones about whom He said: ﴿So Allah came upon them﴾. Thus "So Allah came upon them" here is the coming of His command, exalted is He, which was promised at the beginning of the matter when the command to pardon and overlook was given.
The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, cited at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾ that this verse concerns the People of the Book, as is clear from the context, and said: "The 'amr' in His saying 'bi-amrihi' — some scholars said it is the singular of 'awamir' (commands), and some of them said it is the singular of 'umur' (matters)."
So according to the first view, that it is the command which is the opposite of prohibition, the command mentioned is the one expressly stated in His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29].
And according to the view that it is the singular of "umur" (matters), it is what Allah has stated in the verses indicating what befell the Jews of killing and dispersal, as in His saying: ﴿So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts. They destroy their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O you with vision﴾ and ﴿Had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them﴾ — the verse [al-Hashr: 2–3], and other verses. The verse is not abrogated (ghayr mansukhah) according to verification. End of quote [from the first part of al-Adwa'].
He, may Allah have mercy on him, stated explicitly that the verse ﴿Pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾ is linked to the verse ﴿So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect﴾; that, as we have previously stated, is the promised command, and He has come upon them with it from where they did not expect. What bears witness to all of this is the second reading (fa-ataahum) with a madd, meaning: He gave them and brought down upon them, and the verb would then be transitive with its object omitted, indicated by His saying: (p-19) ﴿from where they did not expect﴾, i.e., He brought down upon them punishment, humiliation and disgrace that came to them from where they did not expect. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.
* *
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾.
Its explicit meaning is that terror was one of the causes of the defeat of the Jews, and the concept by contrary implication (mafhum al-mukhalafah) indicates that the reverse applies in reverse: that tranquility, which is the opposite of terror, is one of the causes of victory, which is the opposite of defeat.
This concept has been expressly stated in verses of the Book of Allah, exalted is He, among them His saying: ﴿Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾ [al-Fath: 18]. Among them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah had already given you victory in many battlefields and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth constricted for you in spite of its vastness, then you turned back fleeing﴾ [al-Tawbah: 25] ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved; and that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 26]. They turned back fleeing in defeat, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down troops of angels, and victory was theirs, and the defeat of their enemies, indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and punished those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Tawbah: 26], i.e., by killing and captivity on that day.
Among them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you do not support him, Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two; when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest; and Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40].
This position is a sign from the signs of Allah: two unarmed men challenging the entirety of Quraysh with its numbers and its equipment; they went out under the shade of swords, and entered the cave in the darkness of the night, and the pursuit came to the mouth of the cave with hearts full of rage, drawn swords, and attentive ears, until the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looked beneath his feet he would see us." He (ﷺ) said, while in the utmost tranquility and the height of serenity: "What do you think of two whom Allah is the third of?"
Among them: and at the most dangerous of positions in Islam, at the Battle of Badr, when truth met falsehood face to face, the forces of evil came in their arrogance, vanity and insolence, and before them were the soldiers of Allah in their humility, their faith, and their supplication to Allah: ﴿So He answered you, "Indeed I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another." And Allah did not make it except as glad tidings and so that your hearts would be reassured by it. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise﴾ ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him, and sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it and remove from you the evil of Satan and to strengthen your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet﴾ [al-Anfal: 9–11].
Allah did not make the reinforcement with angels except so that their hearts would be reassured; and the drowsiness that covered them was only a security from Him; and all of that was completed by what He bound upon their hearts, so they resisted with their small number the forces of evil despite their multitude, and victory was completed from Allah with help from Allah, just as He bound the hearts of the People of the Cave: ﴿And We fortified their hearts when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will never call upon any god other than Him; we would have certainly spoken an enormity"﴾ [al-Kahf: 14].
These are the effects of tranquility, serenity, and the binding upon hearts, indicated by the concept by contrary implication from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect, and cast terror into their hearts; they destroy their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾. Allah, exalted is He, combined the two matters, the explicit and the implicit, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When your Lord inspired to the angels, "Indeed I am with you, so strengthen those who believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]. He stated tranquility through strengthening in His saying: ﴿so strengthen those who believed﴾, and He stated terror in His saying: ﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾. So tranquility became strengthening for the believers, and terror became quaking for the disbelievers.
It has also come in a hadith that when Jibril, peace be upon him, commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to proceed toward Banu Qurayzah, he said: "I will go ahead of you to shake their feet beneath them." Among what indicates the causes of this tranquility in these positions is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much that you may be successful﴾ ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength departs; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Anfal: 45–46].
Thus Allah, exalted is He, mentioned four causes of tranquility:
The first: steadfastness (al-thabat), which is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as if they were a solid structure﴾ [al-Saff: 4].
(p-21) The second: remembrance of Allah much, which is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28].
The third: obedience to Allah and His Messenger, for which His saying, exalted is He, is evidence: ﴿And when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting at death; so woe to them﴾ ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾ [Muhammad: 20–21].
The fourth: not yielding, holding fast, and unity, which is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And hold fast to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided﴾ [Al 'Imran: 103].
From mentioning the causes of defeat as the terror of hearts, and the causes of victory as tranquility and serenity, you can know the extent of the influence of propaganda in recent times, and what has been called the cold war of talk and rumor-mongering, against which one should be extremely cautious. Allah, exalted is He, warned against it in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Already Allah knows those among you who hinder and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us," and they do not come to battle except a little﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], and He warned against listening to them in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had they gone out among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption, and they would have scurried between you seeking discord among you, and among you are listeners to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47].
When the matter became severe for the Muslims in the Battle of the Confederates, and it reached the Messenger (ﷺ) that the Jews had broken their covenant, he sent to them someone to ascertain their news, and instructed him that if they saw treachery, he should not declare it openly, but should speak to him in allusion (lahn), to preserve the tranquility of the Muslims and to remove rumor from their ranks.
As Allah, exalted is He, also showed the effect of good propaganda in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them﴾ [al-Anfal: 60]. And this indeed happened with the departure of the army of Usamah after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the Highest Companion (al-Rafiq al-A'la), and when the Bedouins were waiting in ambush, it had a great effect in thwarting the intentions of those lying in wait against the Muslims, and they said: "They would not have dispatched this expedition unless they had sufficient armies and the necessary strength."

The most practical example of this kind in the Battle of Badr is what Allah made happen there, which is the greatest practical proof: each side was made to appear few in the eyes of the other, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few. And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed over the matter, but Allah saved you. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾ ﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and made you appear few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah are returned all matters﴾ [Al-Anfal: 43-44]. All of this is something that should be benefited from today against the enemy in the cause of Islam and the Muslims.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 4 (part 1 of 2):

Allah's statement: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger﴾.

Al-mushaqqah (opposition, defiance) means disobedience. From it comes the expression "shaqq al-'asa" (splitting the staff, i.e., breaking unity), and it also means opposition.

This indicates that Allah, exalted is He, inflicted what He inflicted on the Banu al-Nadir, namely their expulsion from their homes and the destruction of their houses, because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. It also indicates that the opposition mentioned is the 'illah (effective cause, ratio legis) of the punishment that befell them. There is no doubt that opposing Allah and His Messenger is among the greatest causes of destruction.

In the verse there is a legal-theoretical (usuli) question, based on the fact that opposition occurred from non-Jews, yet that punishment did not befall them, as happened to the polytheists, which is stated in Allah's statement: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels: "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike above the necks and strike from them every fingertip."﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]. This was at Badr, definitively. Then He said: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.﴾ [al-Anfal: 13]. When the Prophet (ﷺ) gained power over the people of Makkah, he did not inflict upon them what he inflicted upon the Jews of killing, but said: "Go, for you are the freed ones." Thus the attribute, which is opposition, which is the 'illah of the ruling, was present, but the ruling, which is expulsion from the homes and the destruction of the houses, was not present.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: If it is said: "If opposition were the 'illah of this destruction, it would be necessary to say: wherever this opposition occurs, destruction occurs. And it is known that this is not so." We say: This is one of the things that indicate that the specification of an explicitly stated 'illah (takhsis al-'illah al-mansusah) does not invalidate its soundness. End of quote.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, examined this issue in his work Adab al-Bahth wa al-Munazarah (Etiquette of Inquiry and Debate), and in Mudhakkirat al-Usul (Memorandum on Usul al-Fiqh), in the section on naqd (counter-example against a cause). In Adab al-Bahth he titled it: "The non-fulfilment of a ruling is not a naqd, whether because of the presence of a mani' (impediment) or the absence of a shart (condition)."

He gave an example of the non-fulfilment of a ruling due to the presence of an impediment: a father killing his son intentionally, yet he is not executed for it in retaliation (qisas), because the 'illah of qisas is present, which is intentional killing, while the ruling, which is qisas, is not fulfilled.

He gave an example of the non-fulfilment of a condition: theft of less than the nisab (minimum threshold), or theft from outside the hirz (protected place).

Then he said: The third type: the non-fulfilment of its ruling from it, not for any of the reasons we have mentioned. Some of them gave as an example Allah's statement: ﴿And had Allah not decreed for them the exile, He would have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.﴾ [al-Hashr: 3]. They said: This 'illah, which is opposition to Allah and His Messenger, may be present in a people who oppose Allah and His Messenger, while its ruling is not fulfilled from it. This noble verse supports the view of the one who said that a naqd in the science of usul is in fact a takhsis (specification) of the 'illah absolutely, not a naqd against it. He attributed this, in Maraqi al-Su'ud, to the majority, in his statement in the section on objections to evidence in usul:

Among them is the existence of the attribute without the ruling; the scholars of knowledge named it naqd.
The majority, in their view, do not regard it as a defect; rather it is takhsis, and this is what makes it sound.

Up to his statement:

I am not harmed by what I have deduced
if it comes due to the lack of a condition or because of an impediment.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, was shown by some brothers an explanation of his (the Shaykh's) Maraqi al-Su'ud at its beginning, on the author's statement:

One in a period of fatrah (interval without prophets) in the branches, and it is not taken into account.

He spoke about the ruling concerning the people of fatrah, then about the specification of some verses, and from there to the specification of the 'illah.

In this manuscript there appears the following text: Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir of surah al-Hashr, preferred that the specification of the 'illah is like the specification of the text absolutely, citing Allah's statement: ﴿And had Allah not decreed for them the exile...﴾ up to the verse [al-Hashr: 3], and something like this was done to other than the Banu al-Nadir, so He did not do to them what He did to them. And Allah knows best. End of quote.

However, I sought this preference of Ibn Kathir at this verse and did not find it, so let it be examined. Perhaps it is in a work other than the tafsir.

As for what he (may Allah, exalted is He, have mercy on him) reported from some scholars in Adab al-Bahth wa al-Munazarah, namely that the ruling may be non-fulfilled from the 'illah for none of the reasons we mentioned, then what appears to me, and Allah knows best, is that the non-fulfilment of the ruling from the 'illah in the case of non-Jews is only due to the non-fulfilment of a part of it, and that the 'illah is (p-24) compound (murakkabah). That is, in the Jews there is opposition plus an additional element, and that additional element was not present in non-Jews, so the difference arose. This is because the opposition of non-Jews was due to their ignorance and doubt, as Allah indicated concerning them by His statement: ﴿And he presented for Us an example and forgot his creation. He said: "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say: "He will give them life who created them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78-79] up to the end of the surah. They are therefore in need of further clarification. Likewise in His statement at the beginning of surah Sad: ﴿And they wondered that a warner from among them had come to them, and the disbelievers said, "This is a magician and a liar. Has he made the gods a one God? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing." And the eminent among them went forth, saying, "Walk on and persevere in your gods; indeed, this is a thing that is intended. We have not heard of this in the latest religion; this is not but an invention. Has the message been sent down to him from among us?" But they are in doubt about My message.﴾ [Sad: 4-8].

They were in wonder, bewilderment and disbelief that the message should be revealed to him (ﷺ) from among them, while they were in doubt about their affair. Thus they were in need of removing doubt and of establishing the matter. Therefore, when their doubt was removed and they became clear about the matter, they began entering the religion of Allah in multitudes. Whereas the disbelief of the Jews was denial after recognition, so they knew him (ﷺ) ﴿as they know their own sons. And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 146]. He had been named to them in what was revealed, as 'Isa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿And a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [al-Saff: 6]. Yet explanation did not benefit them, but it was envy and denial, as Allah made clear their condition by His statement about them: ﴿Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109],
• and His statement: ﴿A faction of the People of the Scripture wish to mislead you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 69],
• and His statement: ﴿And there was a party of them who heard the speech of Allah and then distorted it after they had understood it while they knew﴾ [al-Baqarah: 75],
• and His statement: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 71].

They were a front of misguidance for the people, distortion of the Book, and confusion of truth with falsehood, all of it deliberately and knowingly, driven by envy and hostility. An opponent whose condition is this has no cure, for the deceiver cannot be trusted, the misleader is not believed, and the envious person is cured only by the removal of the blessing from the one envied. On the other hand, Allah has cut off hope in their belief: ﴿Do you hope that they will believe for you while a party of them used to hear the speech of Allah and then distort it after they had understood it while they knew?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 75]. He also despaired of their belief after their confession against themselves, that their hearts are wrapped up, unreceptive to hearing the truth and seeing the light: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are uncovered." Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe﴾ (p-25) [al-Baqarah: 88].

None of these attributes were present in every non-Jew who opposed Allah and His Messenger. Allah has explicitly stated that they deserved this ruling because of the causes peculiar to them alone, in His statement: ﴿And when We took your covenant: "Do not shed your blood or expel yourselves from your homes." Then you acknowledged and you were witnesses. Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of your own people from their homes, assisting against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, while their expulsion is forbidden to you. Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 84-85].

All of that is a violation of the covenant, treachery in peace, shedding of blood, assisting in sin and aggression, believing in part of the Book and disbelieving in part. These were peculiar to the Jews, so the 'illah was compound, consisting of opposition together with these peculiar attributes. The ruling was stated explicitly here in His statement about them: ﴿So what is the recompense of those among you who do that except disgrace in the life of this world; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah: 85]. Their disgrace in this world was what befell them of expulsion, destruction, and killing.

Whoever has this condition, as has been mentioned, cannot be subject to total eradication by expulsion or killing. Reform is no longer possible among them, and no good is expected from them. Sufficient as evidence of this is that the Banu Qurayzah did not take warning, did not benefit, and did not learn lessons as Allah commanded: ﴿So take warning, O people of vision﴾ [al-Hashr: 2].

The Banu Qurayzah did not heed what befell their brothers, the Banu al-Nadir. So after a single year they resorted to the same treachery and betrayal into which the Banu al-Nadir had fallen. Thus the Jews' being singled out for this ruling was due to that common 'illah, because although others shared with them in opposition, others did not share with them in the other side, of the motives of opposition we have mentioned.

Motives have an effect on the ruling, as in the story of Adam and Iblis. Adam and Iblis shared in the general 'illah of disobedience: Adam was forbidden to approach the tree, and Iblis was commanded to prostrate to Adam along with the angels. Adam ate from what he was forbidden, and Iblis refrained from what he was commanded, so they shared in disobedience, as Allah said about Adam: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred﴾ [Ta-Ha: 121], and said about Iblis: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ [al-A'raf: 12]. But the cause differed. Adam forgot and fell under the whisperings of Satan, and was deceived by Iblis's oath by Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And he swore to them both, "Indeed, I am to you both of the sincere advisers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 21]. His disobedience was due to seduction and whispering: ﴿So Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been﴾ [al-Baqarah: 36].

As for Iblis, his disobedience was with premeditation, out of envy and arrogance, as Allah said: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34]. When Allah addressed him by saying: ﴿"O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Are you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?"﴾ [Sad: 75], he said, in his persistence, envy and arrogance: ﴿"I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ [Sad: 76].

The motives differed, and Iblis had what Adam did not have in the cause of disobedience, and consequently the outcomes differed entirely. As for Adam, when He rebuked him for eating from the tree, by His statement: ﴿And their Lord called to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 22], they immediately returned and acknowledged their sin, saying: ﴿They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 23]. Their punishment was His statement: ﴿He said, "Go down, [some of] you to others as enemies, and for you on earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time."﴾ [al-A'raf: 24].

Thus Adam's descent was temporary, and there followed His statement: ﴿We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance - no fear will there be for them, nor will they grieve."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 38]. So the guidance of Allah reached him, and then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 37].

Iblis's outcome: when God rebuked him for his disobedience, saying: ﴿O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands? Have you become arrogant, or were you among the exalted?﴾ [Sad: 75], his answer was one of arrogance and self-magnification. This is the opposite of Adam's answer when he said: ﴿I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [Sad: 76]. Thus his answer was also the reverse of what was said to Adam: ﴿Get out of it, for you are accursed, and upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgement﴾ [Sad: 77-78].

It is said that what drove Iblis to all of this was envy: he envied Adam for the honour God had bestowed upon him, so he belittled him and behaved arrogantly towards him. He thus fell into disobedience, and its outcome was expulsion.

So too with the Jews: their hidden disease is envy and self-admiration. This led them to disbelief, they fell into treachery, and the outcome was killing and expulsion.

The Shaykh, may God have mercy on him, has explained that this opposition by the Jews is from the corruption on earth which God forbade them, and for which He punished them twice, and He threatened them that if they returned for a third time, He would return to take vengeance upon them. And now they have returned, and opposed God and His Messenger, so God empowered over them the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Muslims.

He, may God have mercy on him, said in the surah "al-Isra'" at His words: ﴿And if you return, We shall return﴾ [Al-Isra': 8]: when God explained that the Children of Israel were decreed in the Book that they would cause corruption on earth twice, and explained the consequences of these two times, God also explained: that if they returned to corruption a third time, He, exalted is He, would return to take vengeance upon them by empowering their enemies over them. This is His words: ﴿And if you return, We shall return﴾. He did not explain here whether they returned to corruption a third time or not.

However, He indicated in other verses that they did return to corruption, by denying the Messenger (ﷺ), concealing his attributes, breaking their covenants, supporting his enemy against him, and other ugly deeds. So God, exalted is He, returned to take vengeance upon them, confirming His words: ﴿And if you return, We shall return﴾. He empowered over them His Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and what happened to the Banu Qurayza, the Banu al-Nadir, the Banu Qaynuqa' and Khaybar occurred: killing, plunder, expulsion, the imposition of the jizya on those who remained, and the imposition of humiliation and wretchedness.

Among the verses indicating that they returned to corruption is His saying: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them, and previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers﴾ ﴿Evil is that for which they sold themselves, that they disbelieve in what God has revealed, out of defiance that God should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants. So they returned with anger upon anger, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 89-90]; and His saying: ﴿The defiantly disobedient. Is it not that every time they make a covenant, a party of them throws it aside?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 100]; and His saying: ﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 13], and similar verses.

Among the verses indicating that He, exalted is He, returned to take vengeance upon them is His saying: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came upon them from where they did not expect, and cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of insight﴾ ﴿And had God not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾ ﴿That is because they opposed God and His Messenger; and whoever opposes God, indeed God is severe in punishment﴾ [Al-Hashr: 2-4], and His saying: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts. A party you killed and a party you took captive﴾ ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their wealth﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 26-27], to the end of the verse. Thus far from him, may God have mercy on him.

This is, from him, may God have mercy on him, an explanation and proof of the difference between the opposition committed by the Jews and the opposition committed by others. Hence the ruling's failure to apply to those other than the Jews who opposed God and His Messenger is due to the absence of some part of the cause in the ruling, as we have previously mentioned. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.﴾

Al-līnah (the palm variety) here: it has been said that it is a general term for palm trees, and this is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir.

It has also been said that it is a particular type of them, namely all kinds except al-Barni and al-'Ajwah only.

Ibn Jarir related from some of the people of Basra who said: al-līnah is derived from al-lawn (color). He said: it was only called līnah because it is a form (fi'lah) from fa'ala, and fa'ala is "al-lawn," and it is a kind of palm; but when the letter before it was broken, it was changed into a yā', etc. This last view is close to what the people of Madinah today practice, where they use the word lūnah for what they do not know to have a specific name. Perhaps the word lūnah is a corruption of the word līnah. Among the people of Madinah there are around seventy kinds of palm.

It has also been said that al-līnah is every tree, because of its softness (lu'ūnatihā) with life.

This verse was revealed concerning the cutting and burning of some of the palms of Banu al-Nadir during their siege, when some of the orchard known as al-Buwayrah was cut down. As Ibn Kathir narrated from the two authors of the Sahihs: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burned the palms of Banu al-Nadir and cut them down, and it was al-Buwayrah. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah﴾, the verse."

Hassan (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

"And the burning at al-Buwayrah spreading far was made light of by the nobles of the Banu Lu'ayy."

Al-Buwayrah is well known today; it is an orchard located to the southwest of the Mosque of Quba.

It has also been said concerning the occasion of its revelation: the Jews said, "O Muhammad, you forbid corruption, so why do you order the cutting of trees?" So Allah revealed the verse.

It has also been said: some Muslims forbade one another from cutting the palms, saying, "They are the spoils of the Muslims." So the Qur'an came down confirming those who forbade cutting them, and permitting those who cut them from sin, and that what was cut and what was left was: ﴿by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.﴾

On these views, Ibn Kathir and others said: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾ means the divine decree (al-idhn al-qadari) and the divine will, as in His saying, ﴿And what befell you on the day the two hosts met was by the permission of Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 166], and His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152].

What appears to be the case, and Allah knows best, is that the permission mentioned in the verse is a legal permission (idhn shar'i), which is derived from the generality of permission in His saying: ﴿Permission has been given to those who are fought against because they were wronged, and indeed Allah is competent to give them victory﴾ [al-Hajj: 39]. This is because permission to fight is permission for everything that fighting requires, based on the principle: commanding a thing is commanding it and what cannot be completed without it.

Siege is a type of fighting, and perhaps among the benefits of a siege is cutting some palms to complete the view, or to tighten the siege, or to humiliate and terrify the enemy during its siege and to make him feel his inability to protect his property and possessions. It may also provoke him so that he rushes out in zeal to defend his property and possessions, thereby exposing his fortresses and making it easy to overcome him, along with other military aims.
