Alert (tanbīh)

The use of "qaddamat" in the past form urges haste in doing deeds and not delaying them, because a person owns only what he has sent forward in the past, while the future is not in his hand and he does not know what will happen in it: ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ [Luqmān: 34]. This is like the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Perform Hajj before you are prevented from performing it," and like the Almighty's saying: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 133], and His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-Ḥashr: 19].

After the exhortation to have taqwa of Allah, and to strive to send forward righteous deeds for the coming day, the warning in this verse came against forgetfulness and abandonment, and against being like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Here it does not specify who those are whom He warned against resembling in this forgetfulness, nor what the forgetting and the causing to forget mentioned here are.

The Qur'an has explicitly stated that those who forgot Allah are the hypocrites, in His saying in Sūrat al-Tawbah: ﴿The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and withhold their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-Tawbah: 67]. This is precisely the description with which they are described in Sūrat al-Ḥashr. His saying "fa-nasiyahum" (so He forgot them) means: He caused them to forget themselves, because Allah does not forget: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 52], and ﴿Your Lord was not forgetful﴾ [Maryam: 64] (p-55).

Also, the forgetting has been ascribed in general to each of the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists. Concerning the Jews, Allah says: ﴿So, because of their breaking of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ [Al-Mā'idah: 13]. Concerning the Christians, He says: ﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ [Al-Mā'idah: 14]. Concerning the polytheists, He says: ﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and diversion and whom the worldly life deceived. So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this, their Day, and as they were rejecting Our signs﴾ [Al-A'rāf: 51]. Thus the warning is directed primarily at the hypocrites and includes with them all those groups, since they all share the root of forgetting.

As for forgetting here, it means abandonment. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly stated this when discussing His saying: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 126]. He mentioned two aspects and said: The Arabs use "forgetting" to mean abandonment even deliberately, and from this is His saying: ﴿He said, "Thus came to you Our signs, but you forgot them; and thus today you are forgotten"﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 126]. So what is meant by this verse is deliberate abandonment. Likewise His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this, their Day﴾ [Al-A'rāf: 51], and His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [Al-Ḥashr: 19], and so on. End of quotation.

As for forgetting which is the opposite of remembrance, namely abandonment without intention, it is not included here, because this Ummah has been excused from being held accountable for it, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 286]. In the hadīth, Allah the Exalted said: "I have done it, I have done it," meaning when he (ﷺ) recited it. And the Sunnah has come: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for me the mistakes of my Ummah, and their forgetfulness, and what they have been forced to do." (ﷺ)

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, clarified this type in order to dispel the appearance of inconsistency, in answering the difficulty concerning Adam's forgetting: was it deliberate or not? And if it was not deliberate, how is he held accountable? He also explained the distinctive features of this Ummah in this matter, may Allah have mercy on him, so refer to his discussion.

When the meaning of the warning against resembling them in forgetting has been made clear, and the meaning of forgetting has been made clear, then how did Allah cause them to forget themselves? Here are excerpts from the statements of the exegetes on this point, for further clarification:

Ibn Kathīr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Do not forget the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, lest He cause you to forget righteous deeds, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed."

Al-Qurṭubī said: "They forgot Allah," meaning they abandoned His command, "so He caused them to forget themselves," meaning that they would not do good for themselves.

Abū Ḥayyān said: "Those who forgot Allah are the disbelievers. They abandoned the worship of Allah, obeying what He commanded and avoiding what He forbade, so He caused them to forget themselves, since they did not strive toward it for deliverance from punishment. This is of the kind of recompense for sin with sin. . . etc."

Ibn Jarīr said: "They abandoned fulfilling the right of Allah which He had made obligatory upon them, and this is of the kind of recompense of the same kind as the deed."

As for al-Zamakhsharī and al-Rāzī, they introduced into this meaning a theological discussion, for they said, regarding the meaning of "they forgot Allah" as the majority said, but regarding the meaning of "so He caused them to forget themselves," they mentioned two aspects: The first is as the majority said. The second: it means He showed them on the Day of Resurrection the terrors in which they would forget themselves, like His saying: ﴿Their glances will not return to them, and their hearts are empty﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 43], and His saying: ﴿And you see people as drunks, but they are not drunk; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [Al-Ḥajj: 2]. End quotation.

This second aspect is not accepted from them, because what they went to is general to all creation on the Day of Resurrection, and is not specific to those who forgot Allah, as the Almighty said in the very verse they cited as evidence: ﴿And you see people as drunks﴾ (p-57), so it is general to all people. And His saying: ﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she has nursed﴾ [Al-Ḥajj: 2]. Distraction is the brother of forgetting, and here it is general to every nursing mother. And: ﴿Every pregnant woman will drop her load﴾ [Al-Ḥajj: 2], which is also general. This is due to the severity of the terror of the Day of Resurrection. Perhaps what led them to mention this aspect, while showing its weakness, is their fleeing from attributing causing to forget to Allah, and in it there is a trace of Mu'tazilite doctrine, as is not hidden.

Since the attribution of causing to forget to Shaytan occurs in some places, as in the story of Moses' companion: ﴿And none made me forget it except Shaytan, that I mention it﴾ [Al-Kahf: 63], and as in His saying: ﴿And if Shaytan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-An'ām: 68], and His saying about the companion of Joseph: ﴿So Shaytan caused him to forget the mention of his Lord﴾ [Yūsuf: 42].

However, the correct view among the scholars of the early generations (al-Salaf) is that the reality of forgetting, causing to forget, reminding, and being reminded is like the reality of any meaning, and that all of them are from Allah: ﴿Say, "All is from Allah"﴾ [Al-Nisā': 78], and ﴿Say, "Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us"﴾ [Al-Tawbah: 51]. So what is attributed to Shaytan is by Allah's empowerment, as in His saying: ﴿And they learn from the two what they use to separate between a man and his wife﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 102], then He said: ﴿But they cannot harm anyone thereby except by permission of Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 102]. Thus the attribution of causing to forget to Shaytan is of the kind of the statement of the Friend (Abraham), upon him be peace: ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ [Al-Shu'arā': 80], as courtesy in address toward Allah, the Exalted. But this context is one of information from Allah about what He brought upon those who forgot what He had commanded them, so He caused them to forget. He imposed forgetting upon them regarding themselves as recompense for their deeds. Therefore attributing it to Allah, and by information from Allah, is the very truth, and it is stronger than the style of correspondence: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [Al-Tawbah: 67].

Two alerts (tanbīhān)

The first: In a context like this, there came in the same manner His saying: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this, your Day"﴾ [Al-Jāthiyah: 34]. And His saying: ﴿So taste, for having forgotten the meeting of this, your Day. Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾ [Al-Sajdah: 14]. And His saying: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [Al-Tawbah: 67]. In this is the attribution of forgetting to Allah, the Exalted, and so a difficulty arose with His saying: ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾ [Maryam: 64], and His saying: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 52].

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, answered this in dispelling the appearance of inconsistency: that the forgetting affirmed is in the sense of abandonment, as previously mentioned, while the forgetting negated of Him, the Exalted, is that which means inattention (sahw), because that is impossible for Allah, the Exalted.

The second alert: Among what the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, stated in the introduction to Al-Aḍwā' is that among the types of clarification (bayān) is that there exists in a verse a difference among the scholars, and there exists in it an indicator (qarīnah) that points to the intended meaning. This is present here in this issue, namely His saying: ﴿Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this, your Day﴾ [Al-Jāthiyah: 34]. This statement will be on the Day of Resurrection, and forgetting has been expressed with the present-tense form, which is for the present or the future. Forgetting reported in the present cannot be except by intention and will, and likewise one cannot report forgetting that will occur in the future except by intention and will. This applies to forgetting in the sense of deliberate abandonment. As for that which means inattention (sahw), it occurs without intention or will, so it is not valid to express it with the present-tense form, nor to report its being inflicted upon them in the future. Thus it is established that every forgetting attributed to Allah is in the sense of abandonment, and His saying: ﴿So He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [Al-Ḥashr: 19] is an explanation and clarification of the meaning of: ﴿Today We forget you﴾ [Al-Jāthiyah: 34], and of His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾ [Al-Sajdah: 14]. And Allah knows best.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the ones who will be triumphant.﴾ This noble verse indicates that the two groups, the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise, are not equal. This is a matter known by immediate necessity (badaha), but its mention came as an alert because of people's extreme heedlessness of it, and because of actions that appear from some of them which contradict this self-evident fact, like the one who wrongs his father and is told: "He is your father." This was stated by some of the exegetes.

In the style of eloquent discourse (uslub al-bayan), this is intended to convey the necessary implication of the statement, i.e. it follows from this alert that they should do what keeps them far from the Fire and makes them among the companions of Paradise, so that they may attain the triumph.

Similar examples of this kind of expression occur many times in the Qur'an, such as the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth? Or shall We make the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28] (p-59). And His words: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal﴾ [As-Sajdah: 18], meaning: in judgment with Allah, and not in reality in this life or the Hereafter, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, that their living and their dying will be equal? Evil is that which they judge﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 21]. And here likewise: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾ [Al-Hashr: 20] in rank, station and final destination.

Abu Hayyan said: This is an explanation of the contrast between the two groups, the companions of the Fire in the Hellfire and the companions of Paradise in bliss. The verse, according to the majority of exegetes, explains the comparison between the two groups, and this is the apparent context, as evidenced by His words in it: ﴿The companions of Paradise are the ones who will be triumphant﴾ [Al-Hashr: 20]. This is a ruling that one of the two groups attains triumph, and its implication is a ruling that the second group is destroyed and lost. The preceding verse also supports this: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah﴾ [Al-Hashr: 19], i.e., from this group, so He made them forget themselves, and they became the companions of the Fire, as will be explained later, if Allah wills.

Here there is another possibility: that the companions of the Fire are not equal within the Fire, nor are the companions of Paradise equal within Paradise, in the varying levels they are in, as Abu Hayyan indicated at the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And good and evil are not equal﴾ [Fussilat: 34]. However, the absence of the lam (for emphasis/negation of both sides) here makes this possibility weaker; otherwise He would have said: "The companions of the Fire are not equal, nor are the companions of Paradise." This meaning, although it does occur, given the differing degrees of the people of Paradise in Paradise and the abodes of the people of the Fire in the Fire, its possibility is not applicable here, because the end of the verse passes judgment on the totality of one of the two groups, namely the companions of Paradise, i.e., in their totality, as if it were said: "The Fire and Paradise are not equal, so their companions are likewise."

Abu al-Su'ud noted the priority given to the companions of the Fire in mention over the companions of Paradise, that it is to show at first glance that the deficiency came from their side, as in the words of Allah: ﴿Are the blind and the seeing equal, or are the darknesses and the light equal?﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 16]. End quote.

The explanation of this is that the difference between two things that differ in increase and decrease may be considered as a difference relative to the deficiency in the deficient one, and it may be considered relative to the increase in the one that has more.

So He placed first the deficient side, to show that the disparity which arose between them is caused by the deficiency that came from them, not by an excess in the second group. The result of this is that the deficient side cannot argue against the side of excess, and in this there is greater reproach to the deficient side. In the verse there is a general mention of the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise.

It is known that the word "ashab" (companions) indicates specificity, as if He said: "The people of the Fire and the people of Paradise, those specifically belonging to them."

The Qur'an has shown that the companions of the Fire are the disbelievers, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [At-Taghabun: 10].

Eternity (khulud) has no exit with it, as in His words, the Exalted: ﴿And among the people are those who take other than Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah... ﴾ up to His words: ﴿And those who followed said, "If only we had another return, we would disassociate from them as they have disassociated from us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will never leave the Fire﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 165–167], and as in His words in Surah "al-Humazah": ﴿He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal﴾ ﴿No! He will surely be thrown into the Crushing Fire﴾ ﴿And what can make you know what the Crushing Fire is?﴾ ﴿It is the Fire of Allah, kindled﴾ ﴿Which rises over the hearts﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is closed down upon them﴾ [Al-Humazah: 3–8], meaning: closed shut upon them.

As for the companions of Paradise, they are the believers, as in the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein forever, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 13–14]. He has combined both categories in His words: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and is encompassed by his error, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever. And those who believe and do righteous deeds, those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 81].

Such a complete and matching context has also come, interpreting one part by another as we have already presented, in Surah "at-Tawbah," where Allah, the Exalted, said about the hypocrites: ﴿The hypocrite men and women are of one another; they enjoin what is wrong, forbid what is right, and withhold their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever; it is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is a lasting punishment﴾ [At-Tawbah: 67–68].

These are the categories of disbelief and hypocrisy. Specifically, the companions of the Fire are those who abide therein forever, cursed by Allah, and it is sufficient for them; they are those who forgot Allah, so He forgot them, and they are the very ones mentioned in this surah, Surah "al-Hashr." Then there came a complete contrast in the same context in His words: ﴿The believing men and women are allies of one another; they enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those – Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Almighty and Wise﴾ ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence (Adn), and approval from Allah is greater. That is the great achievement﴾ (p-61) [At-Tawbah: 71–72].

These are also the most distinctive attributes of the people of Paradise: mercy, approval, eternity, and permanent residence in the Gardens of Eden, since 'adn means permanent residence, and from it comes "ma'dan" (mine/source), for the permanence of its residence in its place. And approval from Allah is greater.

Then the conclusion in both contexts is unified: the judgment of triumph for the companions of Paradise. In the verse of "at-Tawbah": ﴿That is the great achievement﴾, and in the verse of "al-Hashr": ﴿The companions of Paradise are the ones who will be triumphant﴾ [Al-Hashr: 20]. By this it is known who the companions of the Fire are and who the companions of Paradise are.

The connection of this contrast between these two groups is made clear, and with what came before them of those who forgot and so Allah made them forget themselves, and those who feared Allah and sent forward for their tomorrow. By this it is known that the sinful Muslims are not included here among the companions of the Fire, for what we have presented: that the companions of the Fire are those specifically belonging to it from among those who disbelieved in Allah and denied His signs. As this is also supported by His words: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass through it; it is a decree that is inevitably carried out﴾ ﴿Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [Maryam: 71–72]. The wrongdoers here are the polytheists in their wronging of themselves.

By this the argument of the Mu'tazilah is refuted, who took from this verse that those guilty of major sins do not enter Paradise, on the claim that if they entered it they would be equal with the companions of Paradise.

This is false, as we have presented. And from another side it is refuted: it may be said, if the sinners are eternal in the Fire according to your claim, despite what they had of faith in Allah and righteous deeds, then what is the difference between them and the disbelievers and polytheists? The words of Allah, the Exalted, have already preceded: ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth?﴾ [Sad: 28].

The Shaykh (may Allah have mercy upon him) investigated the question of the remaining of the sinners and their exit from the Fire, and the eternity of the disbelievers therein, in extensive discussion to remove the appearance of contradiction, in Surah "al-An'am," so let one refer to it.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy upon him) derived from this verse that a Muslim is not to be executed for a dhimmi nor for a disbeliever (p-62), because they are not equal. And that disbelievers do not possess the wealth of Muslims by coercion. This was mentioned by az-Zamakhshari.

This, although it is true, its derivation from this verse is open to scrutiny, because it is in the context of comparison regarding the final outcome on the Day of Resurrection.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 59, verse 21:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split apart from fear of Allah. And these are the parables We set forth for mankind, that perhaps they may reflect.﴾

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had We sent down﴾ indicates that He did not send it down, and that it is mentioned as an example, so that people may reflect upon its matter, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if a Qur'an had by it mountains been set in motion, or the earth had been split asunder, or the dead had been made to speak [by it]...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31] to the end of the verse.

The Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) said here: The response to *law* (لَوْ, "if/had") is omitted.

Some scholars said: Its estimated form is "this Qur'an would have been..." etc.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah, may He be exalted, says, magnifying the matter of the Qur'an and showing its elevated status, and that hearts ought to be humbled by it and split apart when they hear it, because of the true promise and the firm warning it contains: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Hashr: 21].

So if a mountain, with all its hardness and sturdiness, were to understand this Qur'an and reflect upon what is in it, it would be humbled and split apart from fear of Allah, may He be mighty and majestic.

So how fitting is it for you, O mankind, that your hearts should not soften, and humble themselves, and split apart from fear of Allah, when you have understood from Allah His command and have reflected upon His Book? For this reason He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for mankind, that perhaps they may reflect﴾ [al-Hashr: 21].

Some people have indeed experienced something of this when hearing verses of the Qur'an. Among that is what Ibn Kathir narrated in Surah "al-Tur" from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) went out patrolling in Medina one night, and he passed by the house of a man from among the Muslims, and found him standing in prayer. He stopped to listen to his recitation, and he recited: ﴿By the Mount [al-Tur]﴾ [al-Tur: 1], until he reached: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to occur, there is none to avert it﴾ [al-Tur: 7–8]. He said: "An oath by the Lord of the Ka'bah, it is true!" Then he dismounted from his donkey, leaned against a wall, and remained for a while. Then he returned to his home, and he remained ill for a month, people visiting him without knowing what his illness was.

(p-63) Al-Qurtubi also mentioned: "Jubayr ibn Mut'im said: I came to Medina to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the captives of Badr. I came upon him reciting in the Maghrib prayer ﴿By the Mount﴾ up to his saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to occur, there is none to avert it﴾. It was as if my heart was split open, and I embraced Islam out of fear of the descent of the punishment. I did not think I would rise from my place before the punishment befell me."

It is also mentioned in the report about Malik ibn Dinar that he heard it and began to tremble until he fainted.

Al-Suyuti, in *al-Itqan*, transmitted the report of Malik ibn Dinar in full in the section on the inimitability of the Qur'an. He said: A group of people have died upon hearing verses of it, and they have been singled out for separate compilation.

A question may arise here: how can this be the effect of the Qur'an if it were sent down upon mountains, while hearts were not affected by it? The Qur'an has answered this in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that, so they were like stones or even harder in hardness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74]. Likewise, they plugged their ears against hearing it, and covered their hearts with disbelief against understanding it, and locked them with their locks, so they said: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered [and cannot be reached]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 88]. Likewise is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. That is, because of turning away, not reflecting, and forgetting. For this reason He, may He be exalted, said about them: ﴿Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24]. These are the causes of the disbelievers' not being affected by the Qur'an, as the poet said:

*"When a man has no sound eye, it is no wonder that he doubts, though the morning is bright."*

By implication through contrary meaning (mafhum al-mukhalafa), it is understood that the hearts of the believers are humbled and their skins soften, as Allah, may He be exalted, stated explicitly in His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating, at which shiver the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]. And His saying, may He be exalted: "Had We sent down" indicates that He did not send it down upon a mountain, so it did not split apart from it.

Something in the Qur'an indicates what would have happened had He sent it down: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72].

This is an explicit text, because the mountains feared to bear the trust, which is the trust of obligation according to the requirement of Allah's address to them.

So if the mountains feared merely from being offered it, how would they be if it were sent down upon them and they were charged with it?

Among these is that when Allah, may He be exalted, manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Musa fell down unconscious. The Qur'an is the speech of Allah and one of His attributes, so it is evidence (shahid), even if not explicit text.

Among them is the explicit text that some mountains, which are stones, do descend out of fear of Allah, due to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, of stones are those from which rivers gush forth, and indeed, of them are those which split and water emerges from them, and indeed, of them are those which descend out of fear of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74].

The Sunnah has also established something similar concerning Mount Uhud, when the Prophet (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman (may Allah be pleased with them both) ascended it, and it trembled with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be still, O Uhud, for upon you are a Prophet, a truthful one (siddiq), and two martyrs."

Whether its trembling was out of fear or out of reverence, all of this indicates that He, may He be exalted, even though He did not send the Qur'an down upon a mountain, [it shows that] had He sent it down upon it, you would have seen it as He said: ﴿humbled, split apart from fear of Allah﴾.

By this it also becomes clear that the response to *law* (لَوْ) in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if a Qur'an had by it mountains been set in motion﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31] is: "this Qur'an would have been..." which is more preferable than their estimate "you would have disbelieved in the Most Merciful." This is because the subject of moving the mountains, their humbling, and their splitting apart is one and the same, and it is what the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) presented there. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for mankind, that perhaps they may reflect﴾.

*Al-amthal* (الأمثال, "parables/examples") is the plural of *mathal* (مَثَل), which is derived from *al-mathal*. The root meaning of *mathal* is standing upright (al-intisab), and the *mumaththal* (مُمَثَّل) in the form of the passive participle means the thing depicted in the likeness of another.

Al-Raghib al-Isfahani said: It is said: "mathula al-shay'" when a thing stood upright and was pictured, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever loves that men should stand before him, let him take his seat in the Fire." *Al-timthal* is the depicted thing, and *tamaththala* means he pictured it, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So he appeared before her as a well-proportioned man﴾ [Maryam: 17].

(p-65) *Al-mathal* is an expression of a statement about one thing that resembles a statement about another thing, where there is similarity between them, so that one of them may clarify the other and depict it, such as the saying: "The summer has wasted the milk," for this statement resembles your saying: "You neglected your affair at the time of possibility." It is in this sense that Allah's parables are set forth, as He said: ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for mankind, that perhaps they may reflect﴾ [al-Hashr: 21].

And in another verse: ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for mankind, and none understands them except the knowledgeable﴾ [al-Ankabut: 43].

*Al-mithal* is used in two ways:

The first: in the sense of *mathal*, such as "the one compared" (mushabbah) and "that to which it is compared" (mushabbah bihi). Some said: Both are sometimes used to express the description of a thing, such as His saying: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised﴾ [Muhammad: 15].

The second: an expression of resemblance to another in some meaning, whatever meaning it may be, and it is the most general of the terms established for resemblance.

That is because *nidd* (نِدّ, "equal rival") is said of what shares only the essence; *shabah* (شَبَه, "likeness") is said of what shares only the quality; *musawi* (مُساوٍ, "equal") is said of what shares only the quantity; *shakl* (شَكْل, "form") is said of what shares only the measure and dimension; and *mathal* is general in all of that.

For this reason, when Allah, may He be exalted, willed to negate resemblance in every respect, He singled it out with mention, saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11]... to the end. End of quotation.

So His statement in defining *mathal* as an expression of a statement about one thing that resembles a statement about another thing, where there is similarity between them, so that one of them may clarify the other and depict it.

They have agreed that the statement is not changed, but is related as it was first said, such as the saying: "The summer has wasted the milk," with a *kasra* on the *ta'* (تَ) addressing a feminine addressee.

So if it were said to a man who neglected the time of possibility and then sought it after it had passed, you would say to him: "The summer has wasted the milk," with a *kasra* on the *ta'* by way of reported speech (al-hikaya).

(p-66) This is among what is called the *isti'arah tamthiliyyah* (الاستعارة التمثيلية, "representational metaphor"), one of the most eloquent styles. Most of the examples in the Qur'an are of the type of *tashbih tamthili* (التشبيه التمثيلي, "representational simile"), which is the comparison of one image with another image, and it is one of the clearest methods of eloquent expression.

The Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) cited a number of them in the fourth part, at His saying: ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example, but man has been most contentious﴾ [al-Kahf: 54]. Among the most important purposes of this type of simile is to depict one image by another, and to make the hidden manifest and the abstract perceptible, as in His saying: ﴿To Him is the true supplication. And those they invoke other than Him do not respond to them with anything, except as one who stretches out his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but it will never reach it﴾ [al-Ra'd: 14].

If you were to consider the example of this person in this state, and in that image with all its parts, extending his hand with fingers spread toward water far from him, while his mouth is gaping in order to drink, you would say: "What benefit does he gain, and when will he taste the water while he is in that state? He will die of thirst and not taste a single drop of it."

Likewise is the state of one who invokes other than Allah, along with what they invoke besides Him: he gains nothing of value, as in His saying: ﴿The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider who makes for herself a home. And indeed, the frailest of homes is the spider's home, if only they knew﴾ [al-Ankabut: 41]. So what protection is there for a person in a spider's home?

Likewise, what benefit is there in the guardianship of other than Allah? Thus is the situation here. The parables are intended to produce an image, so that the judgment may be drawn out by the listener once the image becomes perceptible and tangible. Consider His saying: ﴿They are garments for you, and you are garments for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187], and how in this style He covered and concealed what is shameful, and presented it in the garment of a simile with that by which one protects oneself, and how precisely the meaning of "garment" matches the need of each of the spouses for the other.

As for His saying: ﴿And these are the parables﴾ [al-Hashr: 21], it refers to the examples mentioned shortly before concerning the conduct of the hypocrites with the Jews and the outcomes of their deeds. Likewise, every alliance with non-Muslims, every hostility, and every turning away from what the Master of the Messengers (ﷺ) brought is included.

Likewise, in clarifying the extent of the Qur'an's efficacy and influence, had it been sent down upon the mountains, they would have been humbled and split apart, which calls for reflection upon it and admonition by it. Then there is the example of the two groups in His saying: (p-67) ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [al-Hashr: 19], and the consequence of that in the Hereafter, from the non-equality of the two groups: "the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise."

It seems that the parables here, and the alerting to them, is an indication that those people, by their forgetting Allah and His causing them to forget themselves, became through this forgetting harder than mountains; indeed, the mountains would be quicker to be affected by the Qur'an than they, if they were reflecting.

Abu al-Su'ud said: He intended to rebuke man for the hardness of his heart, his lack of humility when reciting it, and his scant reflection upon it. End of quotation.

Thus, by these examples, the judgment is drawn out by the listener against those heedless, turning-away people, that their hearts are hard like mountains or even harder, as we have already mentioned. This is in contrast to the believers, whose skins and hearts soften at the remembrance of Allah and what has descended of the truth, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating, at which shiver the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Zumar: 23].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 22 (part 1 of 3):

﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.﴾ ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the King, the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic. Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. To Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

In these three verses there is the mention of the statement of tawhid (the declaration of God's oneness) twice, and the glorification of Allah (tasbih) is also mentioned twice. Along with these are mentioned many of Allah's most beautiful names and His exalted attributes. Thus they comprise three of the most important issues of all religions, with all nations and their messengers, because the call of all the messengers is to the oneness of Allah the Exalted in His essence, His names and His attributes, and to His transcendence (tanzih), and to the refutation of the nations' fabrications against Allah the Exalted.

The Jews said: ﴿Ezra is the son of Allah﴾ [9].

The Christians said: ﴿The Messiah is the son of Allah﴾ [9].

The polytheists said: ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾ [al-Anbiya: 26], and ﴿They made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 19], and they said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing﴾ [Sad: 5] (p. 68).

So each of them claimed a partner with Allah, and they said: ﴿Third of three﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 73], and other than that.

Likewise in the matter of transcendence: the Jews said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Al 'Imran: 181], and they said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained; their hands are chained﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64].

The polytheists said: ﴿And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you order us?﴾ and it increased them in aversion. And they attributed to Allah what none of them would accept for himself. ﴿They made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females,﴾ at the very time when ﴿if one of them is given the news of a female, his face becomes dark and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾ [al-Nahl: 58].

This, as you see, is the greatest fabrication against Allah the Exalted, and the Qur'an recorded it against them in His saying: ﴿And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son." They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie﴾ [al-Kahf: 4–5]. And as He said: ﴿Unquestionably, it is from their own falsehood that they say, "Allah has begotten a son," and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-Saffat: 151–152]. And He said, declaring the enormity of their statement: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced a horrible thing. The heavens nearly rupture from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam: 88–92].

So those three verses were a treatment, in general, for those three issues: the oneness of divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah), the oneness of the names and attributes (tawhid al-asma' wa al-sifat), and the transcendence of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, together with the establishment of proofs for them.

They have been gathered together because none of them is complete except with the other two, so that perfection may belong to Allah the Exalted.

Abu al-Su'ud said: "Indeed all perfections, with their multiplicity and diversity, return to perfection in power and knowledge." End of quote.

All of this is fully present in this context. It began with the statement of tawhid, because it is the foundation: whoever believes in Allah alone believes in everything that has come from Allah, and believes in Allah as He deserves, and declares Him transcendent above what is not befitting to Him. Allah said: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity﴾, then He followed it with the proof of His being singled out for divinity, by that which no other shares with Him, in His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾.

This proof is explicitly stated elsewhere as a proof of Allah's unity, in other places, among them His saying: ﴿Your God is only Allah, other than whom there is no deity; He has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 98]. "Encompassed all things" here is equivalent to "Knower of the unseen and the witnessed." Among them also is His saying: ﴿[Shaytan has made their deeds appealing to them] so that they do not prostrate to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare. Allah — there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne﴾ [al-Naml: 25–26], and His saying: ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾ … to His saying: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

This is definitively something no other shares with Him, as He said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. Therefore it is His right over His creation that they worship Him alone, there is no deity except Him. He brought a second proof, which is His saying: ﴿He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Hashr: 22]. He also stated it explicitly as a proof of oneness in His saying: ﴿And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163]. So He is the Merciful of this world and the Compassionate of the Hereafter.

Among His mercy that is specific to Him in this world is His saying: ﴿And it is He who sends down rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy﴾ [al-Shura: 28], and His saying: ﴿So look at the effects of the mercy of Allah — how He brings the earth to life after its death﴾ [al-Rum: 50], meaning: by His sending down rain and the growth of vegetation, which none can do except Him. Therefore it is His right over His creation that they worship Him alone; there is no deity except Him.

He combined the two proofs, knowledge and mercy, together in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

Then the statement of tawhid came a second time: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity﴾, and after it came the comprehensive attributes: ﴿the King, the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic﴾. This proof of His oneness is stated explicitly in another place in His saying: ﴿Say, "O mankind, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you all, [of the One] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death"﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]. So He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth is the true King, of complete dominion, and He alone has the authority to dispose of His dominion as He wills, by giving life and causing death, as He said: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life﴾ [al-Mulk: 1–2]. He is the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security over His dominion, as in His saying also: ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. So al-Qayyum is the Guardian and the One who sustains every soul; the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic. Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him.

Then He brought the greatest proof in His saying: ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾. He alone is singular in creation, bringing into existence, innovation and fashioning. He stated this proof in more than one place, as in His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He has no companion? And He created all things, and He is, of all things, Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 101]. Then He said: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things﴾ [al-An'am: 102].

He also mentioned creation in detail and dominion in summary in His saying: ﴿He created you from one soul and made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight kinds of cattle. He creates you within the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. Then He said: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him; so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. And He said: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things﴾ [Ghafir: 62], then He said: ﴿There is no deity except Him; so how are you deluded?﴾ [Fatir: 3]. He combined dominion and creation together in His saying: ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion, and who created all things and determined them with precise measure﴾ [al-Furqan: 2], and other verses in this meaning.

* * *

Whoever reflects on the Qur'an's proofs for the oneness of Allah the Exalted, and for His power over resurrection — and these two are the most important doctrinal issues — will find that the most important, clearest and most numerous of them is this proof, namely the proof of creation and fashioning.

This proof has come in the Qur'an both in summary and in detail. From the summary is what came concerning the origin of all created things: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16], and His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Mulk: 1], and He said: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82], then He said: ﴿So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83], and He said: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life﴾ [al-Mulk: 1–2], meaning: the Creator of bringing into existence and of non-existence. The creation of non-existence is equivalent in indicating power to the creation of bringing into existence, because if He were not able to annihilate what He brought into existence, the existent would be beyond His control, and that would be a deficiency in the one who brought it into being. This is like someone who produces a weapon today but cannot destroy it or nullify its effect; it may then become the cause of his own destruction. Power is not truly complete except through creation and annihilation together. And He said concerning the creation of the heavens and the earth: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

And He said concerning the creation of the orbits and their arrangement: ﴿And it is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon﴾ [al-Anbiya: 33].

Then concerning the origins of existents on earth, in His saying: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29].

And concerning the origins of the kinds: water, fire, plants and humans. He said: ﴿Have you considered that which you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 58–59].

And He mentioned with it the power of annihilation: ﴿We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 60].

And concerning the origins of plants: ﴿Have you considered what you plant? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63–64].

And concerning the origins of water: ﴿Have you considered the water you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or are We the senders?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 68–69].

And concerning the origins of the development of life: ﴿Have you considered the fire that you ignite? Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producers?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 71–72].

And concerning the animal realm: ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 17], the verse.

For this reason, He praised Himself with this attribute, the attribute of creation, and described the gods of the polytheists with incapacity, as He said: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see, and He placed in the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you, and He dispersed therein every kind of moving creature. And We sent down rain from the sky and caused to grow therein of every noble kind﴾ [Luqman: 10]. Then He said: ﴿This is the creation of Allah; so show Me what those other than Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error﴾ [Luqman: 11].

It is well known that they have not created anything, as He said rebuking them: ﴿Do they associate with Him what creates nothing and is itself created?﴾ [al-A'raf: 191]. And He showed that the two are not equal in His saying: ﴿Is one who creates like one who does not create? Will you not be reminded?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17]. Then He showed the extent of their weakness and incapacity in His saying: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods that create nothing, while they are themselves created, and they possess not for themselves any harm or benefit, nor do they possess death or life or resurrection﴾ [al-Furqan: 3] (p. 72). This is the utmost incapacity. He also set forth this as an example in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them a thing, they could not recover it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought﴾ [al-Hajj: 73]. Thus they truly possess not for themselves any benefit, nor any harm, not even the weight of a fly. In this way you see that the attribute of creation, which He, glorified and exalted be He, possesses, is the greatest proof of the oneness of Allah the Exalted. It includes the attribute of fashioning and knowledge, because every created thing has a form specific to it, and this can only come from knowledge of the unseen and the witnessed, as has preceded.

Likewise, this proof was the strongest of proofs for resurrection, as He said: ﴿Has not man considered that We created him from a sperm-drop, and then he is an open adversary? And he presents for Us an example and forgets his creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is, of all creation, Knowing."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77–79], to the end of the surah.

End of the first part.

And likewise, in His saying, the Exalted, which is explicit and categorical on this matter: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then [We let you reach] your maturity. And among you is he who is caused to die, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and grows every lovely kind of pair﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. Then the Exalted said: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and because He gives life to the dead, and because He is over all things competent. And because the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and because Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves﴾ [al-Hajj: 6-7].

Then the Exalted explained that whoever denies this proof is only an arrogant ignorant one, astray and leading others astray, and that is in His saying immediately after it: ﴿And among mankind is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book, turning aside in arrogance to mislead [others] from the way of Allah. For him in this world is disgrace, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the burning. [It will be said], "This is for what your hands have put forward, and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants"﴾ [al-Hajj: 8-10].

From here, the first call in the Mushaf addressed to all mankind to worship Allah came with the reason that He alone deserves to be worshipped, because He is characterized by the attribute of creating, as the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you that you may become righteous. [He is] the One who made for you the earth a bed and the sky a canopy and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [it]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21-22]. That is: since they are not equals to Him in what He is characterized by, glorified is He, so do not associate them with Allah in His worship.

Thus these attributes of Allah, the Exalted, at the end of this surah, are in truth proofs for establishing the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, in His essence, His names and His attributes, and that He is the one deserving to be worshipped alone, there is no god but Him.

And it is obligatory upon creation to declare Him far above what is unfitting to His majesty, glorified and exalted is He above what they associate. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, because they are among His creatures, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿To Him belong the best names﴾ [Ta-Ha: 8], it did not explain here the meaning of His having the best names, but it explained the meaning of that in Surat al-A'raf in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And to Allah belong the best names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [al-A'raf: 180].

Al-Qurtubi said: Allah, glorified is He, named His names "the best" because they are good to the ears and hearts, for they indicate His oneness, His generosity, His bounty and His grace. And the coming of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿To Him belong the best names﴾ after the enumeration of fourteen of His names indicates that He has more than that, and no limitation or counting of them has come in any verse of the Book of Allah.

And it has come in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise. He is Witr (One) and loves the witr (odd)."

Ibn Kathir listed the hundred, with differences in the narrations.

He mentioned concerning the verse of al-A'raf that it is not restricted to this number, due to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in Musnad Ahmad, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No worry or grief ever befalls anyone and he says: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your female servant; my forelock is in Your hand; Your judgment over me is executed; Your decree over me is just. I ask You by every name which You have named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Noble Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the removal of my grief and the departure of my worry,' except that Allah removes his grief and his worry." The hadith... (end of quotation) [ended with: ا هـ].

The point of evidence in it is clear that Allah has names which He sent down in His books, and names with which He singled out some of His creation, as He singled out al-Khidr with knowledge from Us, and names which He kept to Himself in the knowledge of the unseen, as the hadith of intercession indicates: "then my Lord will inspire me with praises I did not know before." In reality there is no contradiction between the two hadiths.

Because the first concerns a specific number and what follows from it of reward.

And the second hadith concerns the explanation of the categories of His names, the Exalted, in terms of knowledge of them, teaching them and what is sent down of them.

Ibn Hajar mentioned this reconciliation in al-Fath in the Book of Supplications, under the chapter: "For Allah are a hundred names, other than one."

Some scholars have tried to extract the hundred names from the Qur'an, and they added and subtracted for various considerations. He (Ibn Hajar) extensively discussed this topic in al-Fath over fourteen pages, which are indispensable and cannot be transmitted, nor is it suitable to summarize them.

He also mentioned those who devoted works to it separately.

Just as al-Qurtubi mentioned that he authored a work on it. The basis of the discussion revolves around two points:

The first: specifying the hundred intended names.

The second: the meaning of "enumerates them", and in one narration "memorizes them".

I once attended a session of the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him, in his house, together with Shaykh Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah ibn Baz, and he asked him about what is correct regarding this. The summary of what was stated in that session was that the specification did not come with any authentic text, and that enumeration or memorization should not be understood as mere memorization of the words by heart, but rather it is understood as comprehending their meanings and preserving them from distortion, alteration and nullification, and striving to adorn oneself with their good attributes, such as forbearance, pardon, compassion, mercy, generosity and the like, and beware of [the implications of] names such as the Compeller and the Subduer, and be mindful of names such as the Watchful and the Observer; likewise approaching names such as the Oft-Forgiving and the Most Forgiving through repentance and seeking forgiveness, and the Guide and the Provider by seeking guidance and provision and the like.

Al-Qurtubi quoted from Ibn al-Arabi, at His saying, the Exalted: ﴿so call upon Him by them﴾ [al-A'raf: 180], that is: ask Him by His names, so each name is asked for what is fitting to it. You say: "O Most Merciful, have mercy on me; O Provider, provide for me; O Guide, guide me; O Accepter of repentance, accept my repentance upon me." And so arrange your supplication, and you will be among the sincere. End of quotation.

Question

From this statement of Ibn al-Arabi is derived what the jurists say concerning mentioning the name of Allah at slaughter: that one should limit oneself to saying "Bismillah" and not say "al-Rahman al-Rahim", because the name al-Rahman al-Rahim necessitates mercy, and slaughter does not suit it, and the messenger of the soul.

This is supported by what Ibn Qudamah mentioned, that it was established from him (ﷺ) that "when he slaughtered he said: 'Bismillah, wallahu akbar'", that is: Allah is greater, and more capable of you over it, and He is greater than you over you concerning it.

So when a person comprehends the best names of Allah in this manner, he has truly enumerated them and preserved them in using them according to their meanings, and so he is truly among the people of Paradise. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

The coming of these verses at the end of this surah has long held me in wonder, as a concluding and closing passage, and in the style of summary and detail regarding the matters of tawhid, the establishment of proof, and the binding of the people of atheism and denial. I remained for a long time seeking to connect them with what precedes them, but in all that I came across of tafsir I found nothing more than explanation of vocabulary and some remarks which do not penetrate to the depths of the subject, nor cure a sick person in our modern societies, nor remove the doubts of material modernity. So I returned to the surah in its entirety, contemplating its subject, and I found it begins first with the glorification of all worlds to Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, and this is a matter beyond the level of human perception. Then it presents the greatest event witnessed by Medina after the Hijrah: the expulsion of the Jews, which had not been expected, so Allah came to them from where they did not reckon, and they became a matter of lesson and admonition.

Then it comes to the stance of two opposing groups: the group of believers, and the disbelievers.

The first group is represented by the Muhajirun and the Ansar and their brotherhood, affection, mercy, giving, and preference of others over themselves.

The other group is represented by the hypocrites and the Jews, and what there was between them of promises, incitement and encouragement, then their abandonment of them and forsaking them.

(p-76) Thus this was a depiction of two opposing parties, contradictory: the party of the Most Merciful and the party of Satan, and this is the picture of society in Medina at that time.

Then it moves to another comparison between the outcomes of these two parties, their end, and their non-equality, and in that is the establishment of destiny: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal; the companions of Paradise, they are the triumphant﴾ [al-Hashr: 20].

This is the most dangerous issue for every nation, that is: the establishment of its destiny. Then comes the explanation of the reality of the influence of the Qur'an and its effectiveness on created things: even if it were a towering mountain or a deaf stone, if it were sent down upon it, you would see it humbled and split from fear of Allah. Then this [surah] has encompassed the subject of creation and the Creator, the nation and the message, beginning and end, the struggle of truth with falsehood, disbelief and faith, souls in stinginess and generosity, and all of these are practical positions, realistic methods and expressive examples.

﴿And these are the examples We present to mankind that perhaps they will give thought﴾.

So when thought turns to this presentation, moves from one position to another, and contemplates the handiwork of Allah, His power and His signs, it utters His glorification, and knows that He, glorified is He, is Allah, there is no god but Him, knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He knew what the world would be upon before its existence, so He brought it into being according to the requirement of His knowledge of it, and directed it in the manner in which He brought it into being. He knew the forsaking of the hypocrites of the Jews before they incited them, so it was as He knew, glorified is He, and He warned against resembling them. He knew what would be the state of the Qur'an if it were sent down upon a mountain, so He urged the servants to take it, and by His knowledge of the unseen and the witnessed, He is truly Allah alone.

Then once again: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Bestower of Faith, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Superior﴾: another proof in multiple forms and varied evidences for His oneness, glorified is He. The Sovereign, the Pure: the King who is Guardian over His dominion, the Pure, free from every deficiency, dominant over all that is in His entire kingdom, nothing escapes Him, not even the weight of an atom, as the Exalted said: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Mulk: 1].

Here is a pause to reflect on the combination of these attributes together: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Guardian. We find them interconnected and mutually implicating, because a knower who does not possess disposal and does not dominate anything has no effectiveness for his knowledge.

(p-77) And a sovereign who does not know and is not sanctified above deficiency has no dominance over his dominion. So when all of that and these attributes are combined: knowledge, sovereignty, sanctification and dominance, perfection and majesty are achieved, and that is not possible except for Allah alone, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Superior, and no one shares Him in any of that, glorified and exalted is He above what they associate. ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names﴾. And here, at the end of this context, the believer stands in a stance of reverence and glorification of Allah: the Creator is the one who determines before bringing into existence.

And "al-Bari'" (the Originator) is the one who brings into being from non-existence according to the requirement of creation and determination, and not every one who determines something brings it into existence except Allah.

And "al-Musawwir" (the Fashioner) is the one who shapes every existent in the form in which He brought it into being, and no one singles out each individual of His existents with a form specific to it except Allah, the Exalted, as is present in Allah's creation of humans, animals and plants, each in a form specific to it.

Returning once more to the beginning of the context: creation and determination must necessarily be in accordance with knowledge, whether concerning the present and observed or the future and unseen. This belongs to none but Allah alone, the Knower of the unseen and the seen. So His determining is in accordance with His knowledge, and the King, the Holy, the One capable of disposing of His dominion, brings into existence what He determines.

And "al-Muhaymin" (the Guardian, the Watchful Overseer): He directs what He brings into existence according to what He has determined.

﴿He who created, then proportioned, and who ordained, then guided.﴾ The Mighty who cannot be overpowered; the Compeller (al-Jabbar), who compels everything by His will and His determination, and subjects it to His dominance.

(Al-Mutakabbir) the One who is not exalted over by any creature because of His greatness; He is too great to have anyone share His attributes. He is exalted above having anyone equal Him or share with Him in what is exclusively His. Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him.

At the close of the context is the establishment of a binding proof and the drawing out of acknowledgment and submission: ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾. This is the greatest proof, as has preceded, and it is, as he said, a proof of compulsion (dalil al-ilzam), because creation must have a creator. This is a logical proposition that is accepted: every existent must have an originator. He has held them to this in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Were they created out of nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur: 35]. This, by way of dissection and division, is that it is said: either they were created out of nothing, by which He created them, that is, from non-existence. It is known that non-existence creates nothing, because one who lacks a thing cannot give it, and non-existence is not an existential matter such that it could bring an existent into being.

"Or are they the creators?"

Moreover, they know from themselves that they did not create themselves, so the created must have a creator, and He is Allah, exalted: the Creator, the Originator.

And if it were said by the denier: what we observe of the existence of beings such as humans, animals and plants depends for its existence on causes we observe, such as the two parents for animals, and tilling and watering for plants... etc. Then His saying, exalted is He, came: ﴿the Fashioner﴾. So do the two parents possess the power to fashion the fetus as male or female, or in terms of color, height, shortness, and resemblance?

The answer: No, and never. Rather, that belongs to Allah alone. It is He who fashions you in the wombs however He wills, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills. Or He gives them both males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent﴾ [al-Shura: 49-50].

Likewise with plants: the seed is placed and watered with water, and the soil is one and the water is one. So who fashions the shape of the plant: this a star upon the face of the earth, that a stalk upon a stem, this a vine upon a trellis, that a towering palm? When the fruit appears at the first stage of its development, who fashions it in its shape, whether round or elongated or otherwise? And when it ripens, who fashions it in its color, red, yellow, black, green or white? Is it the soil, or the water, or both together? No, and never. It is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. Glory be to Him; to Him belong the most beautiful names; whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, willingly or unwillingly.

Here is a return to the beginning, closing the surah with what it began with, along with a clarification of what necessitates it and what merits it, and the signs of His oneness. Glory be to Him; there is no god but Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
